title: Timed Verifier Completion
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be binary inputs, let $b$ be a bit, and let $T\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $V$, started in its initial configuration on $y$, halts within the specified time $T$ with output exactly the one-bit word $[b]$. Choose any input-head position for $x$, any contents for the work tapes of $S$, any work-head positions for $S$, and any choice word $w$ of length $T+1$. Running the host under $w$ from the verifier-phase configuration initialized from $V$ on $y$ halts with output exactly $[b]$.
hypotheses_covered: Arbitrary contents of the scheduler work tapes
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines and suppose $V$ computes the single-bit output $b$ on a word $y$ within $T$ steps. For every choice word $w$ with $|w| = T + 1$, running the host under $w$ from the verifier-phase start on $y$ halts with output exactly the one-bit string $b$.
